title: Subventions for Community Counselling and Inclusion of Singaporeans Aged 40 and above with Chronic Conditions in Enrolment for Healthier SG Programme
what_it_is: Subventions for Community Counselling and Inclusion of Singaporeans Aged 40 and above with Chronic Conditions in Enrolment for Healthier SG Programme

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment age extension
sections.summary: Asked whether Healthier SG enrolment will be extended to Singaporeans aged 40 and above at its 5 July 2023 launch, given over 24,000 pre-enrolments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in view that more than 24,000 individuals have pre-enrolled for Healthier SG programme during the pre-enrolment exercise for Singaporeans aged 40 and above with chronic conditions, whether the Ministry will consider extending the Healthier SG enrolment to include Singaporeans aged 40 and above when Healthier SG is officially launched on 5 July 2023.

sections.label: Healthier SG phased pre-enrolment
sections.summary: Over 47,000 residents with chronic care needs pre-enrolled since May; enrolment is phased, prioritising chronic conditions then those 60 and above, with extension to ages 40 to 59 hoped for next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We started a Healthier SG pre-enrolment exercise in May this year so that residents aged 40 and above with chronic care needs can continue to be cared for by their regular general practitioner (GP) clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So far, over 47,000 of these residents have been pre-enrolled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will need to do this in phases, to manage the workload of our GP clinics and polyclinics and ensure residents have a positive experience when they enrol to Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will prioritise those with chronic conditions, followed by those aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We hope to extend this to residents aged 40 to 59 sometime next year.

sections.label: Nationwide GP capacity limits
sections.summary: Even with GP clinic capacity, nationwide capacity must be considered and priority given to older residents, making implementation difficult from a systemic perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Even with the GP, if that particular clinic has capacity, we do need to look at the nationwide capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We need to prioritise capacity for those who are older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, from a national perspective, from a systemic perspective, it will be difficult for us to implement this.

sections.label: GP consultation price competition
sections.summary: Private GPs will be encouraged to price consultations competitively through benchmarking, persuasion and more options, with healthcare inflation so far lagging national inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for our more senior ones, we will encourage private GPs to price their consultations and their services competitively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But through benchmarking, persuasion and encouragement, plus giving more options to patients and residents, we hope there would be competitive dynamics that can keep prices in check as much as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So far, healthcare inflation has lagged behind national inflation, and we will try our best to continue to do so.
